I have been trying this app having become a bit disillusioned with Evernote. Evernote seems to have got worse in recent months and the new interface is a step in the wrong direction in my opinion. The app has also become slow and bloated. 

Having subscribed for a trial with Bear I am really impressed with what this service has to offer. Bear is very intuitive but also very powerful. The interface is extremely easy to use and makes it very easy to find what you are looking for straight away. 

I will likely continue my subscription after my free week trial. The premium subscription fees seem well priced and are cheaper than Evernote. Bear does not offer some of the features of Evernote but I appreciate this is a relatively new application and will likely evolve over time. 

One think that would be nice to see is an option to have a password, or even better finger print support. All in all I am very much enjoying using this app and can't wait to see how it evolves. Here's to hoping it doesn't become to over complicated however!

Bear is a beautiful and simple text editor and organiser. And it's quickly become one of my favourite apps. I adore it.

There are a few little bugs, but overall using the app is a fantastic experience.

I'm also a big fan of its subscription pricing model. It means you can download it for free and try it out, and if you like it you can pay for a few extra features like sync and themes. title.label: Bear enters my top five apps (at number 3)

content.label:
Text editors. I must have used a dozen or so over the past five years. Byword has lasted the longest time. Now a text editor called Bear has stolen the crown. It gives me a lovely clean interface coupled with the marvels of markdown.  I especially like the Gotham theme with its sludgy green and blue colour scheme. I do love a dark theme. I find it easier on the eye. 

The lack of a folder structure threw me at first but I now see that tags are far more flexible. The addition of sub tags makes me a really happy bunny. 

I use it as an addition to Pocket, the bookmarking app, since I can add in links very easily as well as images. For quick notes like every time I buy something online. I can add the amount to my accounts app when I get a moment. I even use it to record ideas for short stories. I can then copy the text directly into Scrivener or Ulysses for proper story tweaking. I also like to pre prepare posts for Facebook, blog entry's and reviews. 

It does seem to be a missing a 'select all' option when I try to copy a block of text into say Facebook but the Copy option in the export icon at the top right of the screen does just as well. I always find text selection to be terribly finicky on an iPad/iPhone anyway. 

I am more than happy to pay a small monthly subscription although having to purchase a separate one for my iPhone seems a tad cheeky. 

So it's Bear for me (until something better comes along).
